summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube dependence, with history of gastrojejunal anastomotic ulcer, was directly admitted for recurrent epigastric abdominal pain with nausea and vomiting after oral intake. She was managed conservatively with nothing by mouth, intravenous fluids, intravenous proton pump inhibitor therapy, continuation of tube feeds, antiemetics, and opioid analgesia as needed. Admission laboratory testing was reassuring without leukocytosis or pancreatitis, and over four hospital days her symptoms improved significantly with tolerance of tube feeds and resolution of vomiting. She was discharged home ambulatory and stable on her home medication regimen with tube feeds continued at 50 cc/hr continuous, ondansetron as needed, and a short course of oxycodone for breakthrough pain, with return precautions and surgical follow-up.
